lessons.title: Places in town

items.example: There is a big park.
items.note: Say 'park' for a green place with trees where you can play.

items.example: I go to school every day.
items.note: Say 'school' for the place where students learn.

items.note: Say 'hospital' for the place where doctors help sick people.

image.describe: a neat stone bank building with tall columns and a gold coin emblem

items.note: Say 'café' for a small place where you have tea, juice, or cake.

lessons.title: Where is the bank?
lessons.scenario: Leo holds a map on the balcony and asks Smarty where places are.

items.example: Where is the bank?
items.note: Start with 'Where is…?' to ask where a place or thing is.

items.example: The café is near the park.
items.note: Use 'near' when two places are close together.

items.example: The station is far from here.
items.note: Use 'far' when a place is a long way away.

items.example: I have a new map.
items.note: Say 'map' for a drawing that shows where places are.

image.describe: an unfolded paper town map with colorful paths, green park areas, and small building icons

grammar.title: Where is…? / near / far
grammar.explanation: Ask 'Where is the…?' to find a place. Answer with 'near' when it is close, or 'far' when it is a long way away.
examples: The bank is near the school.
The station is far from the park.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a drawing with paths and places. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A map shows where places are.

practice.prompt: How do you ask where the bank is?
practice.explanation: Use 'Where is…?' to ask about location.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: The café is near the park.
practice.answer: The café is near the park.
options: The café is near the park.
The café is far from the park.
The bank is near the park.
practice.explanation: Listen for 'near the park'.

practice.prompt: Match each word or question with what fits it.
practice.explanation: 'Near' means not far, 'far' means not near, and 'Where is…?' asks where a place is.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: The station is not near. It is ___.
practice.explanation: The opposite of near is far.

practice.prompt: Ask where the library is.
practice.explanation: Put 'Where is' at the start of the question.

practice.prompt: The hospital is close to the school. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: The hospital is ___ the school.
practice.explanation: Use 'near' when two places are close.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Put the words in order: I have a map.

practice.prompt: Say the questions aloud.
practice.text: Where is the supermarket? Is it near?
practice.answer: Where is the supermarket? Is it near?
practice.explanation: Ask both questions clearly.

lessons.title: I can swim
lessons.canDo: Say what you can and can't do
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Omar relax on the balcony and talk about what they can and cannot do.

items.example: I can swim in the park.
items.note: Say 'I can…' to talk about something you are able to do.

items.example: I cannot ride a bike.
items.note: Say 'I cannot…' or 'I can't…' when you are not able to do something.

items.example: Mia can swim.
items.note: Say 'swim' when you move through water using your arms and legs.

image.describe: a happy cat wearing swim goggles swimming in clear blue water

items.example: I can ride a bike to school.
items.note: Say 'ride a bike' when you sit on a bicycle and pedal it.

image.describe: a cheerful cat wearing a helmet riding a bright red bicycle along a park path

grammar.title: can and cannot / can't
grammar.explanation: Use 'can' + verb for ability, and 'cannot' or 'can't' when you are not able. The verb does not change after 'can'.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a cat in water. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: You swim in water.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a cat on a bicycle. Which phrase fits?
practice.explanation: The cat is riding a bicycle: ride a bike.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for 'can swim'.

practice.prompt: Match each sentence with what it means.
practice.explanation: 'I can' means yes you are able; 'I cannot' means no you are not.

practice.prompt: Smarty is not able to ride a bike. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I ___ ride a bike, but I can swim.
practice.explanation: Use 'cannot' when you are not able to do something.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I can ride a bike in the park.
practice.explanation: Put the words in order: I can ride a bike in the park.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: My young sister ___ read a book.
practice.explanation: Use 'can' before 'read' to show ability.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Put the words in order: I cannot swim.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I can ride a bike, but I cannot swim.
practice.answer: I can ride a bike, but I cannot swim.
practice.explanation: Contrast 'can' and 'cannot' clearly.

grammar.title: opposite, between, behind, in front of
grammar.explanation: Use these words to say where a place is: 'opposite' (facing), 'between' (in the middle of two), 'behind' (at the back), and 'in front of' (at the front).
examples: The café is opposite the park.
The bank is between the school and the shop.
The park is behind the school.

practice.prompt: The café faces the park. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use 'opposite' when two places face each other.

practice.prompt: The bank is in the middle of two places. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: Use 'between' when something is in the middle of two things.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: The park is behind the school.
practice.answer: The park is behind the school.
options: The park is behind the school.
The park is in front of the school.
The park is opposite the school.
practice.explanation: Listen for 'behind the school'.

practice.prompt: Match each phrase with what fits it.

pairs.right: not in front of the school

pairs.left: between the bank and the café

practice.explanation: 'Behind' and 'in front of' are opposites; 'between' is in the middle of two places.

practice.answer: My school is opposite the park.
practice.explanation: Say 'opposite' clearly.

turns.example: The bank is between the café and the shop.
